title: Adaptations and Human Impact
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Adaptations and Human Impact Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe adaptations that help plants and animals survive in their habitats; assess the effects of human activities on habitats and ways to protect them, including Indigenous approaches to caring for the land. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Habitats and Communities)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on animal adaptations, habitat change, invasive species and protecting Ontario habitats. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: People can harm habitats, but we can also protect and restore them.
body_html:
How to think about it

An adaptation is a body part or behaviour that helps a living thing survive.

  • Structural adaptations: thick fur, webbed feet, quills, a beaver's flat tail.
  • Behavioural adaptations: migration, hibernation, hunting at night.
  • Habitat loss, pollution and invasive species (like zebra mussels) harm communities.
  • Parks, wildlife crossings, cleanups and taking only what we need help protect habitats.
Example

Why does a snowshoe hare turn white in winter?

it blends in with snow

Answer: camouflage from predators

Example

Is migration a structural or behavioural adaptation?

it is something the animal does

Answer: behavioural

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an animal changes on purpose when its habitat changes.
  • Mixing up migration and hibernation.
  • Thinking all changes to habitats are caused by people.

faq.q: What is the difference between structural and behavioural adaptations?
faq.a: Structural adaptations are body parts, like quills. Behavioural adaptations are things animals do, like migrating.
A living thing brought to a new place where it spreads and harms local species, like zebra mussels in the Great Lakes.
By keeping water clean, saving natural areas, building wildlife crossings and taking only what is needed.

items.q: Which structural feature helps a saltwater crocodile survive in its habitat?
c: a sensitive bill
a skin flap between its front and back legs
grey, hairy leaves
eyes and nostrils on top of its head
items.e: The saltwater crocodile has eyes and nostrils on top of its head to see and breathe while almost hidden underwater.

items.q: Which feature helps a cactus to lose less water?
c: leaves shaped like jugs that trap insects
spines instead of leaves
gill chambers that hold water
a hard shell
items.e: The cactus has spines instead of leaves.

items.q: What do groundhogs do in winter?
c: grow gills
hibernate (sleep deeply with a slow heartbeat)
change into a plant
migrate to the tropics
items.e: Hibernation saves energy when food is scarce.

items.q: A dog pants on a hot day. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it stay safe, because predators find it hard to pick out one fish.
It helps it lose heat and keep cool.
It helps it reach the nectar deep inside flowers.
It helps it protect itself from predators.
items.e: This adaptation helps the dog lose heat and keep cool.

items.q: Building a highway through a forest splits a habitat in two. What is one effect?
c: The forest grows faster.
Animals get more space.
Nothing happens to animals.
Animals cannot move safely to find food or mates.
items.e: Habitat loss and fragmentation harm wildlife.

items.q: What is an adaptation?
c: a feature or behaviour that helps a living thing survive in its habitat
a place to sleep
a kind of habitat
any change in the weather
items.e: Adaptations can be body parts or behaviours.

items.q: Which feature helps a duck to swim in water?
c: webbed feet
a long, curved beak
spines instead of leaves
air spaces in its stems
items.e: The duck has webbed feet.

items.q: A cactus has spines instead of leaves. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it spot predators while it lies in the water.
It helps it protect itself from predators.
It helps it lose less water.
It helps it get nutrients that are lacking in the soil.
items.e: This adaptation helps the cactus lose less water.

items.q: A thorny devil has grooved skin between its spines. How does this feature help it survive?
c: to carry dew and rain to its mouth in the dry desert
to hop long distances to find food and water
to protect the seeds until a bushfire opens them
to detect small animals in muddy water
items.e: This is a structural adaptation: a body part that helps the thorny devil survive.

items.q: How did Indigenous Peoples traditionally care for the land when hunting and harvesting?
c: by removing all predators
by taking everything at once
by draining wetlands
by taking only what they needed so plants and animals could renew
items.e: Respect for the land helps habitats stay healthy.

items.q: A stick insect has a body that looks like a twig. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it warm up its body.
It helps it catch insects.
It helps it hide from predators.
It helps it support itself in the soft mud.
items.e: This adaptation helps the stick insect hide from predators.

items.q: Zebra mussels came to the Great Lakes on ships. Why are they a problem?
c: They clean pollution and help all animals.
They are a native species.
They are producers.
They crowd out and compete with local species.
items.e: Invasive species upset food webs.

items.q: Which action helps protect a wetland habitat?
c: draining the water
keeping garbage and pollution out of it
cutting down the plants
building a parking lot
items.e: Clean water helps the community.

items.q: Which feature helps a pitcher plant to get nutrients that are lacking in the soil?
c: leaves shaped like jugs that trap insects
spines instead of leaves
large, flat leaves that float on the water
prop roots that spread out above the mud
items.e: The pitcher plant has leaves shaped like jugs that trap insects.

items.q: Why are wildlife crossings built over some highways?
c: to give birds a place to nest on cars
to collect rainwater
so animals can cross safely between parts of their habitat
to slow down cars only
items.e: Crossings reduce road deaths.

items.q: Which feature helps a mudskipper to breathe when it is out of the water?
c: gill chambers that hold water
a body that looks like a twig
sharp talons and a hooked beak
breathing roots that stick up out of the mud
items.e: The mudskipper has gill chambers that hold water.

items.q: A pitcher plant has leaves shaped like jugs that trap insects. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it reach the nectar deep inside flowers.
It helps it breathe when it is out of the water.
It helps it get nutrients that are lacking in the soil.
It helps it catch prey that are active at night.
items.e: This adaptation helps the pitcher plant get nutrients that are lacking in the soil.

items.q: Which feature helps a stick insect to hide from predators?
c: breathing roots that stick up out of the mud
sharp talons and a hooked beak
a body that looks like a twig
gill chambers that hold water
items.e: The stick insect has a body that looks like a twig.

items.q: Which feature helps an eagle to catch and tear its prey?
c: air spaces in its stems
gills
spines instead of leaves
sharp talons and a hooked beak
items.e: The eagle has sharp talons and a hooked beak.

items.q: Why does a snowshoe hare's fur turn white in winter?
c: to stay cooler
to blend in with the snow and hide from predators
to swim faster
to see better
items.e: Camouflage helps it survive.

items.q: What is a structural adaptation?
c: something an animal learns to do
the food an animal eats
a body part or body feature that helps an organism survive
a change in the habitat
items.e: Webbed feet and gills are structural adaptations.

items.q: A frog has a long, sticky tongue. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a behavioural adaptation to reach the nectar deep inside flowers
a behavioural adaptation to catch insects
a structural adaptation to catch insects
a structural adaptation to reach the nectar deep inside flowers
items.e: A body part is a feature of its body, so it is a structural adaptation.

items.q: Why do porcupines have quills?
c: to fly
to keep cool
to catch fish
to protect themselves from predators
items.e: Quills are a structural adaptation.

items.q: A duck has webbed feet. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a structural adaptation to swim in water
a behavioural adaptation to swim in water
a structural adaptation to hide from predators
a behavioural adaptation to hide from predators
items.e: A body part is a feature of its body, so it is a structural adaptation.

items.q: How does the colour of a green grasshopper help it in a school field?
c: It blends in with the grass, so birds find it hard to see.
It helps it make food.
It helps it jump higher.
It keeps it cool.
items.e: Camouflage is a structural adaptation.

items.q: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
c: a stick insect with a body that looks like a twig
an earthworm that moves deeper into the soil in dry weather
a pangolin that rolls itself into a tight ball when attacked
a dog that pants on a hot day
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: Some birds have short, strong beaks and others have long, thin beaks. What does this mostly show?
c: The beaks help them keep warm.
The beaks do not do anything.
The birds are the same species.
Their beaks are adapted to the food they eat.
items.e: Seeds need a strong beak; nectar needs a long, thin beak.

items.q: An owl hunts at night. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a structural adaptation to support itself in the soft mud
a behavioural adaptation to catch prey that are active at night
a behavioural adaptation to support itself in the soft mud
a structural adaptation to catch prey that are active at night
items.e: Something the animal does is a behaviour, so it is a behavioural adaptation.

items.q: A spider spins a web. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a structural adaptation to catch insects for food
a structural adaptation to catch and tear its prey
a behavioural adaptation to catch insects for food
a behavioural adaptation to catch and tear its prey
items.e: Something the animal does is a behaviour, so it is a behavioural adaptation.

items.q: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
c: a spider that spins a web
a Hydrilla plant with air spaces in its stems

a pangolin that rolls itself into a tight ball when attacked
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: A small fish swims in large groups called schools. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a behavioural adaptation to protect its soft belly from predators
a structural adaptation to stay safe, because predators find it hard to pick out one fish
a behavioural adaptation to stay safe, because predators find it hard to pick out one fish
a structural adaptation to protect its soft belly from predators
items.e: Something the animal does is a behaviour, so it is a behavioural adaptation.

items.q: Many birds fly south in the fall. What is this behaviour called?
c: camouflage
hibernation
migration
pollination
items.e: They move to find food and warmth.

items.q: Which of these is a behavioural adaptation?

a mudskipper with gill chambers that hold water
a duck with webbed feet
a pangolin that rolls itself into a tight ball when attacked
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: Why does a beaver have a flat tail?

to dig tunnels
to climb trees

items.e: The tail is a structural adaptation.

items.q: Which of these does not help an animal escape from predators?
c: a hard shell
curling up when touched
a body that looks like a twig

items.e: A curved beak helps a bird obtain food.

items.q: A Hydrilla plant has air spaces in its stems. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a structural adaptation to float near the surface where there is more light
a behavioural adaptation to lose less water
a structural adaptation to lose less water
a behavioural adaptation to float near the surface where there is more light
items.e: A body part is a feature of its body, so it is a structural adaptation.

items.q: Why does a stick insect look like a twig?
c: So that it can make food
So that predators find it hard to see it
So that it can keep warm
So that it can swim
items.e: This is called camouflage.

items.q: What is an adaptation?
c: a feature or behaviour that helps an organism survive in its habitat
a place where an organism lives
a change in the weather

items.q: What is a behavioural adaptation?
c: a body part such as a beak

items.q: Why do moose have long legs?

to climb trees
to dig burrows
items.e: Long legs suit their habitat.

items.q: Trees in a rainforest are cut down. Is this change good for wildlife or harmful to wildlife?

good for wildlife
it only affects the weather

items.q: How can people help wildlife in a school garden?
c: cover it in concrete

items.q: Which change could cause this: Frogs and newts lose their habitat.
c: A pond is filled in to build a parking lot.
Fertilizer runs off fields into a lake.
Plastic litter is left on a beach.
Oil leaks into the sea.
items.e: Match the cause to the effect.

items.q: Why should we not drop litter?

It feeds animals well.
It makes no difference.

items.e: Litter is dangerous.

items.q: A river floods after heavy rain. Is this a natural change or a change caused by people?

items.q: Which change could cause this: More bees and butterflies can find nectar.

items.q: What can happen to living things when their environment changes?
c: They all change their bodies right away.

items.q: Noah's class reads: “Dead trees are cleared from a park. Woodpeckers and owls have fewer places to nest.” Which solution would help most?
c: cut down more trees
put out cat food

c: the other class's solution, because it is bigger
Neither, because problems cannot be solved.
Olivia's solution, because it fixes the cause of the problem
Both are equally good.
items.e: A good solution helps the plants and animals affected by the change.

a hot desert
a pond
a tropical rainforest
